name: Guidance
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You touch a willing creature. Once before the spell ends, it can roll a d4 and add the result to one ability check of its choice.
tactics: The most-used cantrip in the game out of combat. +1d4 on any ability check, on demand, forever. AS A CHANGELING PALADIN THIS IS A CHARISMA ENGINE: you have Advantage on Charisma checks while shifted (Shape-Shifter), Wayfarer gives you Insight and Stealth, and your Charisma is your best stat. Add Guidance and you are rolling Persuasion or Deception with Advantage, a high modifier, and +1d4. You are the party face by a wide margin and no other class gets there this cheaply. THE ETIQUETTE PROBLEM: many DMs get tired of 'I cast Guidance' before every check. The fix is to declare it as a standing behavior — 'I keep Guidance up whenever we are investigating' — and let the DM tell you when it is not available. IT IS CONCENTRATION, so it is off in combat when you are running Bless. That is fine; it is not a combat cantrip.

name: Light
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You touch an object no larger than 10 feet in any dimension. Until the spell ends it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. You can dismiss it as an Action. An unwilling creature can make a Dexterity save to avoid being targeted.
tactics: Buy a torch. Genuinely — you get exactly two cantrips from Blessed Warrior and this is not worth one of them for a character with a Darkvision-heavy party. THE EXCEPTION THAT MAKES IT WORTH CONSIDERING: cast it on an ENEMY'S object or on the enemy itself (they get a Dexterity save). A lit-up enemy cannot hide and can be tracked. Against a stealth-based opponent this is a cheap permanent answer. HEARTH FLAVOR: it is thematically ideal — you are the light in the dark. But your Hearthfire Manifest already sheds bright light in 10 feet and dim for 10 more, for free, as a Bonus Action. Light is mostly redundant with your own subclass feature. Take Guidance and Sacred Flame or Toll the Dead instead.

name: Mending
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You repair a single break or tear in an object you touch, as long as the damage is no larger than 1 foot in any dimension. It leaves no trace of the former damage but does not restore magical properties.
tactics: Too situational for one of only two cantrip picks. Repairing a torn map, a broken key, a cut rope, or a snapped chain is genuinely useful once a campaign — and once a campaign is not worth a permanent slot when your alternative is a damage cantrip you use every fight. IF SOMEONE ELSE IN THE PARTY HAS IT, you are covered. Artificers, Wizards, Bards, Clerics, Druids and Sorcerers can all take it. SKIP IT.

name: Resistance
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You touch a willing creature. Once before the spell ends, it can roll a d4 and add the result to one saving throw of its choice.
tactics: Guidance for saves, and much worse than Guidance, because saves happen in combat and combat is where your Concentration is already committed to Bless. THE DIRECT COMPARISON THAT KILLS IT: your Aura of Protection gives every ally within 10 feet a bonus to EVERY save equal to your Charisma modifier — +{CHAmod} at Charisma {CHA}, permanently, on every save, with no Concentration and no action. Resistance gives one ally +1d4 on ONE save and costs your Concentration. Your class feature is strictly better in every dimension. SKIP IT. This cantrip exists for classes that do not have your aura.

name: Sacred Flame
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: Flame-like radiance descends on a creature you can see within range. It must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d8 Radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from Cover for this save. The damage increases at character levels 5, 11 and 17.
tactics: The standard ranged answer for a Blessed Warrior Paladin, and the choice between this and Toll the Dead is the real decision. IT IGNORES COVER — that is Sacred Flame's unique selling point and it is genuinely valuable. An archer behind a wall, an enemy in a murder hole, a caster peeking around a corner: cover normally gives +2 or +5 to Dexterity saves and AC. Sacred Flame ignores it entirely. Against a fortified position this is the only ranged option in your kit that works. IT USES A SAVE, NOT AN ATTACK ROLL, so a high-AC target does not blunt it — but a high-Dexterity target does. It is the mirror image of Scorching Ray: use Sacred Flame against armored, low-Dexterity enemies and Scorching Ray against agile, low-AC ones. RADIANT IS EXCELLENT: rarely resisted, and it is the same type as your Divine Smite and your level 11 Radiant Strikes, which keeps your damage profile consistent. SACRED FLAME VS TOLL THE DEAD: Toll the Dead does more damage (1d12 against a wounded target versus 1d8) and Necrotic is resisted about as rarely as Radiant. Sacred Flame ignores cover; Toll the Dead uses a Wisdom save. Take Sacred Flame if your campaign has fortifications and undead; take Toll the Dead if you want raw numbers. Do not take both — they overlap almost completely and you only get two cantrips. THE HONEST CAVEAT: at level 5+ with Extra Attack, two weapon swings almost always beat one cantrip. This is your answer for the rounds you CANNOT reach melee, not your default action.

name: Spare the Dying
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You point at a creature within range that has 0 Hit Points. It becomes Stable, stopping its death saving throws, though it remains Unconscious.
tactics: Do not take this. You have a strictly better version already. THE COMPARISON: Lay on Hands is a BONUS ACTION and 1 single point from your 35-point pool brings a downed ally to 1 Hit Point and CONSCIOUS — back in initiative, able to act. Spare the Dying costs your whole ACTION and leaves them at 0 and unconscious on the floor. You would be spending an Action to achieve less than you can achieve with a Bonus Action and one point of a resource you regain on every Long Rest. There is no scenario where this is the right button. SKIP IT.

name: Thaumaturgy
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You manifest a minor supernatural sign within range: your voice booms three times as loud, flames flicker and change color, harmless tremors shake the ground, an eerie sound plays, a door or window flies open or slams shut, or eyes glow. You can create up to three effects at once and dismiss them as an Action.
tactics: No combat value and real social value in the right hands — which are yours. THE CHANGELING PALADIN USE CASE: you are a shapeshifter with Advantage on Charisma checks while shifted, playing a character whose oath is about gathering people. Thaumaturgy is the tool that makes an Intimidation or Persuasion check land. Booming voice plus glowing eyes plus the flames in the hearth changing color while you speak is not a mechanical bonus by RAW, but most DMs will grant Advantage on a check backed by a genuine divine manifestation. Ask your DM whether they will. THE FIRE CLAUSE IS PURE OATH OF THE HEARTH: 'flames flicker, brighten, dim, or change color.' You can make every fire in a room respond to you. For a Hearth Paladin that is the single most flavorful cantrip in the game. VERDICT: take it only if your table rewards roleplay mechanically and you already have a ranged answer. Otherwise Guidance plus Sacred Flame or Toll the Dead is the stronger pair.

name: Toll the Dead

damage.dice: 1d8, or 1d12 if the target is missing any Hit Points (scales at character levels 5, 11, 17)

grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: You point at a creature you can see within range and a mournful bell tolls. It must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 1d8 Necrotic damage — or 1d12 instead if it is already missing any Hit Points. The damage dice increase in number at character levels 5, 11 and 17.
tactics: The highest-damage cantrip available to you, and the correct pick if you want raw numbers. THE d12 CLAUSE IS ALMOST ALWAYS ACTIVE: it upgrades from d8 to d12 if the target is missing ANY hit points. In practice, by the time you are casting a cantrip at something, your party has already hit it. Treat this as a d12 cantrip. At level 11 that is 3d12, averaging 19.5 — better than most Paladins' single weapon attack. NECROTIC IS THE RIGHT DAMAGE TYPE FOR A HEARTH PALADIN specifically because your subclass is drowning in Fire and your class is drowning in Radiant. Almost nothing except Undead resists Necrotic, and it gets through Fire-immune AND Radiant-immune enemies. Your kit has a real coverage gap and this is the cheapest way to close it. WISDOM SAVE: strong against Beasts, Constructs, Giants and most brutes; weak against Clerics, Fey and Aberrations. The opposite profile from Sacred Flame's Dexterity save, which is why picking one is a real choice rather than a strictly-better decision. IT DOES NOT IGNORE COVER — the one thing Sacred Flame does that this cannot. RECOMMENDED PAIR FOR YOUR BUILD: Guidance plus Toll the Dead. Guidance turns your already-excellent Charisma into party-face dominance out of combat; Toll the Dead gives you a hard-hitting ranged option in a damage type nothing in your kit otherwise covers.

name: Word of Radiance
grantedBy: Optional pick: Blessed Warrior Fighting Style (Paladin level 2) grants any TWO Cleric cantrips; Charisma is the spellcasting ability
summary: Burning radiance erupts from you in a 5-foot Emanation. Each creature you choose in that area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 1d6 Radiant damage. The damage increases at character levels 5, 11 and 17.
tactics: The only cantrip that scales with how surrounded you are, which makes it uniquely suited to a front-line Paladin who wants to be surrounded. 'EACH CREATURE YOU CHOOSE' MEANS IT NEVER HITS YOUR ALLIES. You can be in a melee scrum with your whole party and detonate safely. That is rare and valuable. THE MATH AGAINST EXTRA ATTACK: at level 7 you make two weapon attacks for roughly 20 damage to one target. Word of Radiance at level 5+ is 2d6 (avg 7) to every enemy within 5 feet. You need three or more adjacent enemies before it beats attacking, and even then your attacks are more reliable. SO WHY TAKE IT: because it is the ONLY way a Paladin damages a crowd before level 9 (Fireball) or level 17 (Destructive Wave). Against a swarm of six kobolds, zombies, or stirges surrounding you, this is a real answer where your greatsword is not. THE HEARTH PLAY: walk into the middle of the pack — you have heavy armor, Aura of Protection, Aura of Solace, and at level 13 Fire Shield and Hearthfire Manifest punishing everything that hits you — then detonate. Being surrounded is your win condition, not your problem. This cantrip rewards that posture more than any other. CONSTITUTION SAVE IS THE WEAKNESS: it is the save most enemies are best at. Expect a lot of misses. VERDICT: a good third pick you cannot afford. With only two cantrips, take Guidance and one ranged damage cantrip. Consider Word of Radiance over the ranged option only if your campaign is swarm-heavy and your party already has ranged coverage.

name: Bless
higherLevel: Target one additional creature for each slot level above 1.
summary: Up to three creatures you can see add 1d4 to every attack roll and every saving throw they make for the duration. You must hold Concentration to keep it running.
tactics: The single best use of a level 1 slot you have that is not a Smite, and the math says so: 1d4 (avg 2.5) on every attack from four party members over three rounds is worth far more than one 2d8 Divine Smite. Cast it in round one BEFORE you close to melee, because from round two onward your Bonus Action wants to be Divine Smite and your slot budget is one per turn. POSITIONING: Bless has a 30-foot range at cast time but NO ongoing range limit — once it lands, allies can scatter across the whole battlefield and keep it. So cast it while the party is still stacked at the entry point, then spread out. STACKING: Bless does not stack with itself, but it DOES stack with your Aura of Protection. At level {level} with Charisma {CHA} that is +1d4 and +{CHAmod} to every save inside 10 feet of you — a party standing in your aura under Bless is passing saves it would otherwise fail, all fight long. That is the single largest force multiplier a level {level} Paladin can put on the table. RISK: it is Concentration. Take Resilient (Constitution) or War Caster if you intend to lead with Bless, and stand where you will eat one big hit rather than five small ones — every hit is a separate Concentration save.

name: Burning Hands
grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 3 - always prepared
summary: A sheet of flame shoots from your outspread fingers in a 15-foot Cone. Each creature in the area takes 3d6 Fire damage, or half as much on a successful Dexterity save. It also ignites flammable objects in the area that no one is holding or wearing.
tactics: Your only crowd-clearing option until level 17's Flame Strike, and at level 7 it is worth more than it looks. THE MATH VERSUS TWO WEAPON ATTACKS: at level 7 with Extra Attack you swing twice for roughly 20 damage to ONE target. Burning Hands upcast to level 2 is 4d6 (avg 14) to EVERY creature in a 15-foot cone. Against three enemies that is 42 damage for one Action and one level 2 slot. Two or more targets and the spell wins; one target and it loses badly. Count heads before you cast — that is the entire decision. THE POSITIONING PROBLEM AND THE FIX: a 15-foot cone from Self means you must be adjacent to the pack, and a cone from your position will usually catch your own melee allies too — Burning Hands does NOT let you exclude friends. Solve it by being the one who charges the group first, before your party engages. Round one, ride in, detonate the cone, and let your allies mop up from outside the blast. This requires you to be comfortable standing surrounded, which is exactly what your heavy armor, Aura of Protection and Aura of Solace are for. IT SETS FIRE TO THINGS. Read the ignition clause and use it — burn a rope bridge behind you, light an oil slick, set a wooden barricade alight, torch a field between you and pursuers. Terrain damage is a legitimate tactic and this is the only spell you have that does it. FIRE IS THE MOST-RESISTED DAMAGE TYPE IN THE GAME. Against devils, fire elementals, red dragons and most demons, this spell does half or nothing. Always carry a non-Fire answer — Wrathful Smite (Necrotic) and Divine Smite (Radiant) are yours. AT LEVEL 15 SMOLDERING SMITE MAY CHANGE THIS. If your DM rules the subclass's Fire damage to ignore resistance broadly, ask whether it applies here too. As written it does not — see the errata file.

name: Command
higherLevel: Target one additional creature for each slot level above 1.
summary: You speak a one-word command to a creature that can hear and understand you. On a failed Wisdom save it spends its next turn obeying: Approach, Drop, Flee, Grovel (falls Prone), or Halt (does not move). It cannot be commanded to do something directly harmful to itself.
tactics: A slot-efficient tempo weapon that most Paladins forget they own. HALT on the enemy's melee bruiser buys your back line an entire round for one level 1 slot. DROP disarms a boss with a magic weapon and forces it to spend an object interaction or an action to recover. GROVEL knocks a target Prone at 60 feet with no attack roll, giving your whole melee line Advantage next round — which is worth more than the damage of the Smite you did not cast. POSITIONING: FLEE is the underrated one. A fleeing enemy provokes Opportunity Attacks from everyone it runs past. Use it to drag a caster out of its own party's protective cluster and into your line. WEAKNESS: it is Wisdom-save-only, and it is Charisma-DC-dependent. At level {level} with Charisma {CHA} your DC is {saveDC} — that lands on brutes and fails on clerics and fey. Read the target before spending the slot.

name: Compelled Duel
summary: One creature you can see must succeed on a Wisdom save or be compelled to fight you. While the spell lasts it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against anyone but you, and it cannot willingly move to a space more than 30 feet from you. The spell ends if you attack anyone else, harm anyone else with a spell, or end your turn more than 30 feet from the target.
tactics: This is the Paladin's true tanking button and almost nobody uses it. 5e/5.5e has no threat mechanic — you cannot MAKE things attack you — except through this spell. It converts you from a durable body into an actual Defender. THE KEY INSIGHT: it costs a Bonus Action, which means on the turn you cast it you cannot Divine Smite. Accept that trade. Round one you spend the Bonus Action on Compelled Duel; every round after, the boss is swinging at your 20 AC with Disadvantage while you Smite it, and your wizard is untouched. Over four rounds that is worth vastly more than one 2d8. DISCIPLINE REQUIRED: the spell ends the moment you attack anyone else. That means no Cleave, no Destructive Wave, no attacking the adds. You are committing to a duel — say so out loud at the table so your party knows to handle the trash. POSITIONING: the 30-foot leash cuts both ways. Cast it, then WALK BACKWARD toward a chokepoint. The target must follow you or break the compulsion's movement clause, so you can physically drag a boss away from your downed ally and into your party's kill zone. Combine with the Push weapon mastery to hold it at exactly the distance you want. AURA SYNERGY: pulling one big threat 30 feet away from the fight also pulls it OUT of range of the allies who are standing in your 10-foot Aura of Protection — you become the only thing inside its reach, which is exactly what a Hearth Paladin is for.

name: Cure Wounds
summary: Touch a creature and restore 2d8 + your Charisma modifier Hit Points. It has no effect on Constructs or Undead.
tactics: Almost always the wrong button for a Paladin, and your app should say so plainly. Lay on Hands is a BONUS ACTION and costs no spell slot — Cure Wounds costs your entire Action plus a slot for a comparable amount of healing. Spending your Action to heal means giving up two attacks plus a Smite. WHEN IT IS ACTUALLY RIGHT: (a) your Lay on Hands pool is empty; (b) you need burst healing bigger than the pool can deliver in one Bonus Action; (c) you are out of melee range of anything worth hitting anyway. THE REAL RULE FOR A PALADIN: 1 point of Lay on Hands as a Bonus Action gets a downed ally back on their feet and back into initiative. That is the highest-value healing in the game because it restores an entire turn to your side. Never spend a whole Action topping off a conscious ally.

name: Detect Evil and Good
summary: For the duration you sense the presence of Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, and Undead within 30 feet, and you know what type each one is. You also sense consecrated or desecrated places and objects. It does not tell you location through Total Cover.
tactics: A scouting tool, not a combat spell, and it is largely redundant with your Channel Divinity. IMPORTANT OVERLAP YOUR APP SHOULD FLAG: Divine Sense (your free level 3 Channel Divinity) does most of this for free at 60 feet as a Bonus Action for 10 minutes. Detect Evil and Good adds Aberrations, Elementals and Fey to the list and does not burn a Channel Divinity use — that is the entire reason to prepare it. In a Fey or Aberration campaign it is worth a slot; otherwise use Divine Sense and prepare something else. TACTICAL USE: it detects through thin walls. Walk a corridor with this running and you know which door has the Fiend behind it before you open it — that is an ambush you set instead of one you walk into.

name: Detect Magic
summary: You sense magic within 30 feet. Spending a Magic action to study a specific aura tells you its school of magic. Total Cover blocks the sense.
tactics: 2024 CHANGED THE MATH ON THIS: ritual casting is no longer a class feature you need to unlock. Any character with a Ritual-tagged spell prepared can cast it as a Ritual, taking 10 minutes longer and spending NO spell slot. Paladins can now ritual-cast. That makes Detect Magic effectively free out of combat and worth one of your seven prepared slots on any dungeon-crawling day. PARTY ROLE: if your Wizard or Cleric already has it, do not prepare it — your prepared list is only seven spells and it is the tightest resource you own. If nobody else does, take it: identifying which door is warded before you touch it is how parties stop losing characters to traps.

name: Detect Poison and Disease
summary: You sense poisons, poisonous creatures, and diseases within 30 feet, and you identify what each one is.
tactics: Narrow, but it is a Ritual, so it costs nothing but ten minutes. Prepare it on a day you expect to be eating, drinking, or negotiating with someone who might not want you to leave the table. REAL VALUE: it identifies WHICH poison or disease, which tells your party whether Lesser Restoration (you have it) or Protection from Poison (you have it) is the right answer, and whether the problem is on a two-hour clock or a two-week one. Knowing that is usually worth more than the detection itself. DEFAULT RECOMMENDATION: do not keep it prepared. Swap it in on a long rest when you know you are walking into a banquet, a plague town, or a swamp.

name: Divine Favor
summary: For 1 minute your weapon attacks deal an extra 1d4 Radiant damage on a hit. No Concentration required.
tactics: The correct comparison is against Divine Smite, and the math is closer than people think. THE MATH AT LEVEL 7: you have Extra Attack, so two hits per round. Divine Favor adds 1d4 (avg 2.5) per hit for 10 rounds. Divine Smite is a one-time 2d8 (avg 9). Divine Favor breaks even after four hits — two rounds. In any fight lasting three or more rounds, one Divine Favor out-damages one Divine Smite. WHY IT IS STILL USUALLY SECOND CHOICE: it costs your Bonus Action on the turn you cast it AND consumes your one spell slot for that turn, which means the round you cast it you deal LESS damage than normal. You are buying a future advantage with present tempo. WHEN TO ACTUALLY CAST IT: (a) round one of a fight you know is long — a boss with legendary actions, a siege, a horde; (b) when you are out of high-value Smite targets and just need consistent chip damage; (c) crucially, it is NOT Concentration, so it stacks with Bless from your Cleric and with Crusader's Mantle. A Paladin running Divine Favor while standing in an ally's Bless is adding +1d4 damage and +1d4 to hit on every swing. HEARTH NOTE: Divine Favor is Radiant. Your oath is fire-themed but your class chassis is radiant — that is a feature, because almost nothing resists both.

name: Divine Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a target with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

damage.bonus: +1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead

grantedBy: Paladin level 2 (Paladin's Smite) - always prepared; one free cast per Long Rest with no slot
summary: Immediately after you hit with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you spend your Bonus Action to channel 2d8 extra Radiant damage into that hit, plus another 1d8 if the target is a Fiend or Undead.
tactics: THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN YOUR ENTIRE KIT, AND THE ONE APPS GET WRONG: 2024 says 'On a turn, you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell.' You cannot cast Bless and then Divine Smite in the same turn. You cannot Smite twice in a turn. One slot, one turn, no exceptions. THE LOOPHOLE THAT IS ACTUALLY LEGAL: your level 2 Paladin's Smite feature lets you cast Divine Smite once per Long Rest WITHOUT EXPENDING A SLOT. The one-slot rule restricts EXPENDING slots. So on one turn per long rest you can legally cast a slotted spell with your Action and free-cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action. Save that turn for the round you need to open hardest. SMITE AFTER YOU SEE THE ROLL: you cast this AFTER the hit is confirmed, not before. Never pre-commit. Attack, see the number, then decide. This is the single biggest reason Divine Smite beats Searing Smite on efficiency — no wasted slots on misses. CRITICAL HITS DOUBLE THE SMITE DICE: on a crit you roll all the attack's damage dice twice, and the Smite dice are part of that attack's damage. A crit with a level 2 slot is 6d8 of Smite. So SMITE ON CRITS, ALWAYS, without hesitation, even against a target you would not otherwise spend a slot on. ATTACK ORDER DISCIPLINE: with Extra Attack you get two swings. Take the first swing. If it crits, Smite immediately. If it hits normally, hold — take the second swing, and if THAT crits, Smite it instead. You only get one Smite per turn either way, so let the dice tell you which hit deserves it. TARGET PRIORITY: Fiends and Undead take +1d8. Concentrating enemy casters are the real prize — a big Smite forces a Concentration save at DC 10 or half the damage, and a 2nd-level Smite averaging 13 means a DC 10 save, while a crit for 27 means a DC 13. Dropping an enemy's Wall of Force or Hold Person is worth more than the raw damage. UNARMED STRIKES COUNT: the casting time explicitly names Unarmed Strikes. If you are grappling something and cannot draw a weapon, you can still Smite it. RANGED IS OUT: no bows, no crossbows. Thrown melee weapons (javelin, handaxe) are a genuine RAW dispute — make this a configurable toggle in your app and ask your DM which way it rules. HEARTH SYNERGY (level 15): Smoldering Smite adds 1d8 Fire that ignores resistance AND immunity. Note your subclass text says 'Magic action to cast Divine Smite' — that is a homebrew error, Divine Smite is a Bonus Action spell in 2024 and never a Magic action. See the errata file.

name: Faerie Fire
grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 3 - always prepared
summary: Each creature in a 20-foot Cube within range is outlined in light of a color you choose unless it succeeds on a Dexterity save. Affected creatures shed Dim Light in a 10-foot radius, cannot benefit from the Invisible condition, and attack rolls against them have Advantage.
tactics: The best action-economy spell your oath gives you at level 3, and the one most Paladins underuse. ADVANTAGE FOR THE WHOLE PARTY ON A 20-FOOT CUBE. Not one target — a cube. Catch three enemies and every attack your party makes against any of them has Advantage for a minute. Advantage is worth roughly +5 to hit. Across a four-person party over three rounds that is a larger damage swing than any Smite you can cast at this level, by a wide margin. DEXTERITY SAVE, NOT CONSTITUTION — this is why it lands. Most heavy brutes, undead, oozes and constructs have poor Dexterity. It is the opposite of your Smite spells' save profile, which makes it the right opener against exactly the enemies your Smites struggle to debuff. IT IS A HARD COUNTER TO INVISIBILITY AND HIDING. 2024 folded hiding into the Invisible condition, and Faerie Fire explicitly stops a creature from benefiting from Invisible. Rogues, drow in Darkness, invisible stalkers, anything that keeps vanishing — Faerie Fire ends the problem for a minute. It also works on a target you cannot see, because it targets an AREA. Blanket the square you think the assassin is standing in. THE OPENING ROUND DOCTRINE FOR A HEARTH PALADIN: round one, cast Faerie Fire from 60 feet as you close. It costs your Action but not your Bonus Action, so you can still summon your Hearthfire Manifest. From round two you are in melee with the whole party swinging at Advantage. That is a better round one than walking up and hitting something once. CONCENTRATION COST: this is the trade. Faerie Fire competes with Bless and Shield of Faith. Rule of thumb — Faerie Fire when there are three or more enemies clustered, Bless when they are spread out. IT DOES NOT COUNT AGAINST YOUR PREPARED SPELLS. Free, always ready, and it is not on the normal Paladin list, so your oath is genuinely giving you something you could never otherwise have.

name: Heroism
summary: A willing creature you touch becomes immune to the Frightened condition and gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Charisma modifier at the start of each of its turns. The temp HP vanish when the spell ends.
tactics: At Charisma {CHA} that is {CHAmod} temp HP refreshed every single turn for ten rounds, all of it bought with one level 1 slot. Nothing else at this level mitigates that much. PUT IT ON THE RIGHT TARGET: the instinct is to self-cast. Resist it. You have d10 hit dice, heavy armor, Lay on Hands, and an aura. Your Rogue or Wizard does not. Those refreshing temp HP on a d6-hit-die caster are proportionally three times the value they have on you. THE HEARTH CONFLICT YOUR APP MUST WARN ABOUT: Temporary Hit Points do not stack. When you gain new temp HP you choose to keep the old pool or take the new one. Your Hearthfire Manifest cloak grants temp HP and its fire retaliation lasts 'until the Temporary HP is depleted.' If you are wearing the cloak and then someone casts Heroism on you, taking the new temp HP replaces the cloak's pool and — by the feature's own wording — likely ENDS your cloak. Never run Heroism on yourself while cloaked. This is a hard rules interaction, not a judgment call, and your app should block or warn on it. ANTI-FEAR STACK: Frightened immunity is redundant with your Aura of Courage at level 10 — until then, Heroism on your most fear-vulnerable ally covers the gap.

name: Protection from Evil and Good

components.materialText: a flask of Holy Water worth 25+ GP, which the spell consumes

summary: One willing creature you touch is warded against Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, and Undead. Those creature types have Disadvantage on attack rolls against the target, and they cannot Charm, Frighten, or possess it.
tactics: Read the component line before you prepare this: it CONSUMES 25 GP of holy water every cast, and a Spellcasting Focus cannot substitute for a consumed component with a listed cost. Your app must track holy water as consumable inventory or this spell will silently break. WHEN IT IS THE BEST SPELL IN YOUR BOOK: a single-boss fight against a Fiend, Undead, or Fey. Disadvantage on every attack against the target for ten minutes is roughly a 25%% reduction in incoming hits — better than any AC bonus you can buy at this level. STACKING FOR A HARD TANK: Protection from Evil and Good (Disadvantage to be hit) + Compelled Duel (Disadvantage to hit anyone but you) does not double-dip on the same roll — Disadvantage does not stack. But they cover different targets: Protection makes YOU hard to hit, Compelled Duel makes the enemy hit ONLY you. You cannot run both, they are each Concentration. Pick by the shape of the fight: Compelled Duel when the party is the thing that will die, Protection when you are. ANTI-POSSESSION IS THE HIDDEN VALUE: it blocks possession outright. In any campaign with ghosts, intellect devourers, or demonic influence, this spell is the only thing standing between your Fighter and a TPK from the inside.

name: Purify Food and Drink
summary: All nonmagical food and drink in a 5-foot-radius Sphere within range is rendered free of poison and disease.
tactics: Ritual, so it costs nothing but ten minutes. Nearly useless in combat and quietly excellent at a negotiating table. HEARTH THEMATIC NOTE: this is the most on-oath spell in your entire list. 'Gather to the hearth those in need of warmth and rest' — you are literally the character who can feed a starving village safely. Pair it with Create Food and Water at level 9 and you can sustain a refugee column indefinitely. That is not a combat play, it is the thing that makes your character matter between fights. PRACTICAL: keep it OFF your prepared list day to day; swap it in on a long rest before a feast, a siege, or a plague scenario. Seven prepared spells is too tight to hold a utility ritual permanently.

name: Searing Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

damage.note: on the hit, then 1d6 Fire at the start of each of the target's turns until it succeeds on the save

save.when: end of each of the target's turns

higherLevel: Both the initial and ongoing damage increase by 1d6 per slot level above 1.
summary: Your hit sets the target alight. It takes 1d6 Fire damage immediately, and 1d6 Fire again at the start of each of its turns until it succeeds on a Constitution save to put the fire out. Not Concentration.
tactics: THE HEARTH PALADIN'S SIGNATURE LEVEL 1 SPELL, and the numbers back the flavor. HONEST MATH: guaranteed damage is only 2d6 (the hit plus one tick) versus Divine Smite's 2d8, and Fire is the most commonly resisted damage type in the game. On raw expected damage against an average enemy, Divine Smite wins. WHERE SEARING SMITE ACTUALLY WINS: (a) it is NOT Concentration, so it runs alongside Bless, Compelled Duel, or Shield of Faith — Divine Smite competes for the same slot but Searing Smite competes for nothing else; (b) it scales better, +2d6 per slot level versus Divine Smite's +1d8; (c) against a low-Constitution target — most casters, most Fey — the ongoing tick is real damage every round; (d) IT BREAKS CONCENTRATION REPEATEDLY. Every tick at the start of the enemy caster's turn forces another Concentration save. One Searing Smite on an enemy wizard can strip three separate concentration spells over a fight. That is the play. THE STEALTH-KILLER: ongoing fire damage means an enemy cannot hide from you. It is taking damage every round and that damage reveals position in most rulings. AT LEVEL 15 THIS BECOMES YOUR BEST SMITE: Smoldering Smite adds 1d8 Fire that ignores resistance and immunity. Read your subclass text carefully — as written it only triggers on Divine Smite, and it uses the wrong action type. Ask your DM to rule it as 'any spell with Smite in its name' and Searing Smite becomes the centerpiece of the build. See the errata file. TARGET PRIORITY: enemy spellcasters, Trolls (fire stops their regeneration in most rulings), and anything you expect to run away.

name: Shield of Faith
summary: A shimmering field gives one creature within 60 feet a +2 bonus to Armor Class for the duration.
tactics: Ten minutes of +2 AC for one level 1 slot and a Bonus Action, at 60 feet. That is the best damage-mitigation-per-slot ratio you have. THE AC MATH THAT MATTERS: at level 7 in Plate (18) with a Shield (+2) and the Defense fighting style (+1) you are at 21. Shield of Faith makes it 23. Against a typical CR 7 attacker with +7 to hit, going from 21 to 23 drops their hit rate from 35%% to 25%% — that is nearly a 30%% cut in incoming damage, sustained for the whole fight. CAST IT BEFORE THE FIGHT: ten-minute duration means you can cast it in the corridor, not the doorway. A Paladin who walks into every room already at +2 AC is a different character from one who spends round one buffing. THE CONCENTRATION DECISION — THIS IS THE REAL CHOICE OF YOUR CAREER: you can run exactly one of Bless, Shield of Faith, Compelled Duel, or Protection from Evil and Good. The rule of thumb: Bless when the party's offense is the bottleneck, Shield of Faith when YOUR survival is the bottleneck, Compelled Duel when your party's survival is the bottleneck. Bless is usually right in a party of four or more; Shield of Faith is right when you are alone, escorting, or holding a chokepoint. 60-FOOT RANGE IS THE HIDDEN FEATURE: you can put this on a squishy ally across the room without leaving your position. Most Paladins self-cast it on reflex and waste that reach.

name: Thunderous Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

save.effect: negates the push and Prone only

summary: Your hit rings like thunder for an extra 2d6 Thunder damage. The target must also succeed on a Strength save or be pushed 10 feet away from you and knocked Prone.
tactics: You give up an average of 2 damage versus Divine Smite to buy a push and a knockdown. In a party with any melee at all, that is a bargain. WHY PRONE IS WORTH MORE THAN 2 DAMAGE: a Prone enemy has Disadvantage on its own attacks, gives Advantage to every attacker within 5 feet, and must spend half its movement to stand. In a party with three melee attackers, one knockdown converts roughly six attack rolls to Advantage — worth far more than 2 points. THE PUSH COMBO — THIS IS THE REAL PLAY: pair Thunderous Smite with the PUSH weapon mastery (Greatclub, Pike, Warhammer, Heavy Crossbow). Push moves the target 10 feet on a hit with no save; Thunderous Smite moves it another 10 and knocks it down. That is 20 feet of forced displacement plus Prone in a single turn. A 30-foot-speed enemy then spends 15 feet standing up and has 15 feet left — it cannot reach you. You have removed an entire enemy turn. BATTLEFIELD CONTROL: forced movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from you, but it CAN shove a target off a ledge, into your Wall of Fire (level 13), into a Spike Growth, or out of its own healer's range. Look at the terrain before you pick your Smite. AS A HEARTH PALADIN: pushing enemies AWAY from the people you are guarding is the mechanical expression of your entire oath. This is your control button.

name: Wardaway
summary: A burst of repelling force strikes one creature. On a failed Constitution save it takes psychic damage and has its Speed halved until the end of its next turn; on a success it takes half damage and is not slowed.
tactics: NOT IN THE CORE 2024 PLAYER'S HANDBOOK. This comes from a later Forgotten Realms supplement — confirm with your DM that the book is in play before you build around it, and have your app flag it as optional/expansion content rather than baseline canon. IF IT IS LEGAL AT YOUR TABLE: it is a rare ranged option for a class that has almost none, but it is Constitution-save-based, which is the save most monsters are best at. Weak in practice. REALISTIC VERDICT: skip it. Your seven prepared spells are too scarce for a mediocre ranged debuff. If you need a ranged answer, take Blessed Warrior as your Fighting Style and pick up Sacred Flame or Toll the Dead instead — cantrips cost no slot and no prepared-spell slot.

name: Wrathful Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

save.when: end of each of the target's turns

summary: Your hit deals an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage and the target must succeed on a Wisdom save or be Frightened of you for the duration, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.
tactics: The lowest damage of any Smite and the strongest debuff. Frightened means Disadvantage on all its attacks AND it cannot willingly move closer to you. THE LOCKOUT COMBO: Frightened enemies cannot move toward you. Combine with the PUSH weapon mastery — push the target 10 feet away, and now it is Frightened and physically unable to close the distance. It has to either use ranged attacks at Disadvantage or spend its turn doing nothing. Against a pure melee brute, one Wrathful Smite can neutralize it for the entire fight for a single level 1 slot. TARGET PRIORITY: low-Wisdom melee creatures — Beasts, Constructs (check immunity), Giants, Ogres, most Undead grunts. Never spend it on a caster or a Fiend; they will make the save. NECROTIC IS THE RIGHT DAMAGE TYPE MORE OFTEN THAN YOU THINK: almost nothing except Undead resists it, and it goes through Fire-immune enemies — which matters a great deal for a Hearth Paladin whose subclass damage is all Fire. Keep one non-Fire answer prepared at all times. This is it. AURA INTERACTION: at level 10 your Aura of Courage makes your allies immune to Frightened. Enemies get no such protection — Wrathful Smite works fine.

name: Aid

healing.note: raises current and maximum Hit Points by 5

higherLevel: +5 to both current and maximum HP per slot level above 2.
summary: Three creatures within range each have their Hit Point maximum AND their current Hit Points raised by 5 for 8 hours. No Concentration.
tactics: CAST THIS AT BREAKFAST. Eight-hour duration, no Concentration, three targets. Cast it after every Long Rest and it is running for the entire adventuring day at the cost of one level 2 slot. Fifteen effective hit points spread across the party, permanently, for one slot, is the best value-per-slot in your book. THE COMBAT TRICK MOST PEOPLE MISS: Aid raises CURRENT hit points as well as maximum. A creature at 0 HP is at 0 current HP — so casting Aid on a downed ally instantly brings them to 5 HP and conscious. With three targets and 30 feet of range, Aid can revive up to three downed allies with a single Action. That is a party-saving emergency button, not just a buff. THE TRAP: Aid does not stack with itself. Recasting at the same level does nothing; you must use a higher slot. And if the spell ENDS while a creature is below 5 hit points, its maximum drops back and it falls unconscious. Your app must track the eight-hour timer and warn when Aid is about to lapse on a wounded character. HEARTH DOCTRINE: this is the most Oath-of-the-Hearth spell in your kit — the buff you put on your found family every morning before you walk out the door. Treat casting it as a ritual of the oath, and it will never feel like a wasted slot.

name: Find Steed
higherLevel: The steed's statistics improve; use the slot's level as the spell's level in its stat block.
grantedBy: Paladin level 5 (Faithful Steed) - always prepared; one free cast per Long Rest with no slot
summary: You summon a loyal spirit that takes the form of a Celestial, Fey, or Fiend mount (Warhorse, Pony, Camel, Elk, Mastiff, or similar). It obeys you, fights alongside you, and its Hit Points and statistics scale with the level of the slot used. It vanishes when it drops to 0 HP and can be resummoned.
tactics: You get this ALWAYS PREPARED and FREE ONCE PER LONG REST at level 5. If you are not summoning your steed every single day, you are throwing away a free level 2 spell. THE FREE-CAST LOOPHOLE: like Paladin's Smite, the free casting expends no spell slot. Since the 2024 restriction is 'you can expend only one spell slot on a turn,' the free Find Steed does not count against it. SPEED IS THE POINT, NOT THE MOUNT'S ATTACKS: a Warhorse has 60 feet of movement. Mounted, you close from 60 feet away and still attack — a Paladin's biggest structural weakness is that all your damage is melee and you spend round one walking. Mounting solves it. On a controlled mount, the mount moves on your initiative and you still get your full Action, Bonus Action, and Smite. AURA ON HORSEBACK: your 10-foot Aura of Protection moves with you. A mounted Paladin can reposition the aura 60 feet per round — you can ride to whichever ally is about to fail a save and blanket them. That is the single strongest thing a level 7 Hearth Paladin can do with movement. THE STEED AS A TOOL, NOT A PET: it has an Action of its own you can direct. Use it to Dash a downed ally out of an area of effect, to body-block a corridor, or to Help (granting Advantage) on your own attack against a boss. SCALING: cast with a higher slot for a tougher steed. At level 7 you only have level 2 slots, so your steed is at its base durability — do not ride it into a dragon's breath. Dismount before big AoE, remount to chase. TELEPATHIC BOND at 1 mile makes it the best scout in the party.

name: Gentle Repose

components.materialText: 2 copper pieces, which the spell consumes

summary: A corpse you touch is protected from decay and cannot become Undead. The 10-day duration also does not count against the time limit of spells that raise the dead.
tactics: A Ritual, so it costs no slot — only ten minutes and two copper. There is almost never a reason not to cast it on a fallen ally. THE MECHANIC THAT SAVES CHARACTERS: Revivify only works within 1 minute of death. Raise Dead works within 10 days. Gentle Repose PAUSES that clock. Cast it on your dead friend and you now have ten days of real time to find a diamond and a caster who can bring them back, instead of one minute of panic. STACK THE DURATIONS: spell durations can overlap even though spells do not stack. Recast Gentle Repose on day nine and the preservation continues without a gap. You can hold a body indefinitely. COMBAT-ADJACENT USE: it prevents a corpse from rising as Undead. In a necromancer fight, ritual-casting it on the enemy's most dangerous fallen minion between waves denies them a resource. HEARTH DOCTRINE: your oath is about protecting found family. This is the spell that says you do not leave anyone behind, even dead. Prepare it the moment you know you are entering somewhere lethal.

name: Lesser Restoration
summary: You touch a creature and end one condition on it: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. It also ends one disease affecting the target.
tactics: NOTE THE CASTING TIME — 2024 made this a BONUS ACTION. In 2014 it cost your whole Action. That change turns it from a niche utility spell into a mid-combat rescue you can fire off while still attacking. Your app must not show this as an Action. PARALYZED IS THE REASON TO PREPARE IT: a Paralyzed ally auto-fails Strength and Dexterity saves and every hit against them within 5 feet is an automatic critical. Against ghouls, carrion crawlers, or a Hold Person, an ally who stays Paralyzed for two rounds usually dies. Ending it as a Bonus Action while you still take the Attack action is a whole character saved for one slot. REACH THE TARGET FIRST: it is Touch range. Plan your movement so you end adjacent to whoever went down. This is where mounted movement and your steed's Dash matter. OVERLAP CHECK: Lay on Hands already removes Poisoned for 5 points, and at level 14 Restoring Touch adds Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed and Stunned to Lay on Hands for 5 points each. Until level 14, Lesser Restoration is your ONLY answer to Paralyzed. Keep it prepared. After 14, drop it. IF YOUR PARTY HAS NO CLERIC OR DRUID, this is non-negotiable — you are the only one who can do it.

name: Locate Object
summary: You sense the direction to a specific object you are familiar with, or to the nearest object of a general kind, as long as it is within 1,000 feet. Lead or a thin sheet of lead blocks it.
tactics: Weak in practice and easily countered — anyone hiding something valuable wraps it in lead. It is also Concentration, which for you is a very expensive resource. THE ONE USE THAT JUSTIFIES IT: 'the nearest object of a particular kind' works on categories. Locate the nearest STAIRWAY, DOOR, or LEVER in a maze and you have solved a dungeon. Locate the nearest HOLY SYMBOL and you have found the cult's shrine. Think in categories, not in specific items. DEFAULT RECOMMENDATION: do not keep it prepared. Swap it in on a Long Rest when the session's problem is explicitly 'find the thing.' Seven prepared spells is far too tight for a situational Divination.

name: Magic Weapon
higherLevel: Slot level 3-5: +2 bonus. Slot level 6+: +3 bonus.
summary: A nonmagical weapon you touch becomes a magic weapon with a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls for 1 hour. No Concentration.
tactics: Whether this is your best level 2 spell or a dead slot depends entirely on one question: does your DM hand out magic weapons? Ask before you build. IF YOUR GAME IS LOW-MAGIC, THIS IS ESSENTIAL. A +1 to hit is worth more than it looks — with Extra Attack you make two attacks a round, so +1 to hit is roughly a 5%% increase in landed attacks on both of them, and it also increases how often you crit into a doubled Smite. And it makes your weapon COUNT AS MAGICAL, which bypasses the resistance that most high-CR monsters have to nonmagical weapon damage. That resistance clause is the real prize — against a creature resistant to nonmagical B/P/S, this spell doubles your weapon damage. ONE HOUR, NO CONCENTRATION: cast it before you go in, not in the doorway. It stacks with Bless, with Divine Favor, with Shield of Faith — it competes with nothing. IF YOU ALREADY HAVE A MAGIC WEAPON: do not prepare it. It does not stack, and it would downgrade a +2 weapon. Your app should detect an equipped magic weapon and gray this out.

name: Prayer of Healing

healing.note: also confers the benefits of a Short Rest

summary: Over ten minutes you bless up to five creatures within range. Each regains 2d8 Hit Points and gains the benefits of a Short Rest. A creature can benefit from this spell only once per Long Rest.
tactics: READ THE SHORT REST CLAUSE — that is the whole spell. 2024 added 'the target also gains the benefits of a Short Rest.' That means one 10-minute cast gives five party members a full Short Rest: your own Channel Divinity use back, the Warlock's slots back, the Fighter's Second Wind and Action Surge back, the Monk's ki back. THE STRATEGIC MATH: a normal Short Rest costs an hour of in-world time. This costs ten minutes. In any dungeon on a clock — a ritual counting down, a hostage, pursuit, a siege — compressing an hour into ten minutes is worth more than any combat spell you own. It changes how many encounters your party can take in a day. THE LIMIT: once per creature per Long Rest. You cannot chain it. Spend it at the right moment — usually after the second hard fight, not the first. CASTING TIME RULE: a spell of 1 minute or longer requires you to take the Magic action on every one of your turns and maintain Concentration the whole time. If you are interrupted, the spell fails but you do NOT lose the slot. So it is safe to attempt — just do not attempt it somewhere you might be found. PARTY DOCTRINE: if your app has a rest planner, it should suggest Prayer of Healing whenever the party wants a Short Rest and the clock is hostile.

name: Protection from Poison
summary: You touch a creature. If it is Poisoned, you neutralize the poison. For the next hour it has Advantage on saving throws against being Poisoned and Resistance to Poison damage.
tactics: Poison is the most common damage type across the entire CR range — it shows up at CR 1/8 and at CR 24. A one-hour, no-Concentration Resistance plus Advantage on the save is a genuinely strong defensive buff for one slot. PRE-CAST IT: one hour means it goes on before the fight. If you know you are fighting a green dragon, a swarm of snakes, an assassin, or anything in a sewer, cast it on the party's most fragile member on the way in. IT ALSO CURES: unlike Lesser Restoration this both cures the existing Poisoned condition AND prevents the next hour of it. Lesser Restoration is a Bonus Action and better in combat; this is better before combat and lasts. OVERLAP WITH LAY ON HANDS: 5 points from your Lay on Hands pool removes Poisoned as a Bonus Action, free of slots. So the CURE half of this spell is redundant for you. Prepare it for the PREVENTION half, or not at all. AT LEVEL 13 THIS BECOMES OBSOLETE: Aura of Purity (level 4 spell) gives the same Poison resistance to everyone in your aura plus Advantage against a long list of conditions. Drop this then.

name: Scorching Ray
grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared
summary: You create three rays of fire and hurl them at targets within range. You can send them at one target or several. Make a separate ranged spell attack for each ray; each one that hits deals 2d6 Fire damage.
tactics: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT SPELL YOUR OATH GIVES YOU, because it fixes the Paladin's defining weakness: you have no ranged damage. At 120 feet, three rays, 6d6 potential, this is a real answer to flying enemies, enemies across a chasm, and the round where you cannot close to melee. THE FLYING-ENEMY ANSWER: a Paladin against an airborne target is normally reduced to throwing javelins for 1d6+Strength. Scorching Ray triples that output. If your campaign has dragons, wyverns, or anything with a fly speed, keeping this in mind changes whether those fights are frustrating or fine. THE ATTACK-BONUS PROBLEM YOU MUST UNDERSTAND: each ray is a separate ranged SPELL attack using your Charisma-based spell attack modifier, not your weapon attack. At level {level} with Charisma {CHA} that is +{spellAttack}. Against a well-armored target you will miss with most rays. Scorching Ray is at its best against LOW-AC targets and at its worst against armored ones — the opposite of your weapon attacks. Read AC before choosing. SPLIT OR FOCUS — THE REAL DECISION: three rays at one target maximizes the chance of killing it. Three rays at three wounded enemies maximizes the chance of finishing multiple. Focus for bosses, split for clean-up. A ray that overkills a 4-HP goblin is wasted. IT IS AN ACTION, NOT A BONUS ACTION. Casting it means no Attack action that turn, and because of the one-slot-per-turn rule it also means no Divine Smite. Only cast it when you genuinely cannot reach melee — otherwise two attacks plus a Smite is more damage. FIRE RESISTANCE IS THE HARD COUNTER. Against fire-immune enemies this spell does literally nothing. AT LEVEL 15, ASK YOUR DM ABOUT SMOLDERING SMITE. If it is ruled to cover all your oath's Fire damage rather than only Divine Smite, Scorching Ray becomes resistance-piercing and jumps to the top of your kit. As written it does not apply. See the errata file. DOES NOT COUNT AGAINST YOUR SEVEN PREPARED SPELLS — it is free capability, permanently.

name: Searing Orb
source: Post-launch official digital release (D&D Beyond Drops, 2026)
summary: You hurl a mote of searing light. Make a ranged spell attack; on a hit the target takes Radiant damage and must succeed on a Constitution save or be Blinded until the end of your next turn.
tactics: NOT IN THE PRINTED 2024 PLAYER'S HANDBOOK — this is a later official digital addition. Confirm your DM allows post-launch content, and have your app tag it as expansion rather than core canon. IF LEGAL: it is one of the only true ranged attack options a Paladin has ever had, and Blinded is a strong condition — Disadvantage on the target's attacks, Advantage on everyone's attacks against it. THE HONEST PROBLEM: a Paladin's spell attack bonus is Charisma-based, and you are usually standing in melee where you would rather make two weapon attacks plus a Smite. Spending your Action on one ranged spell attack is a damage loss in almost every round you could reach the enemy. WHEN IT IS RIGHT: flying enemies you cannot reach, a target across a chasm, or a boss you need Blinded before it uses a gaze attack or a breath weapon. VERDICT: a good emergency answer to the Paladin's ranged weakness, but do not keep it prepared over Aid or Magic Weapon. If you want a permanent ranged option, take Blessed Warrior for cantrips instead.

name: Shining Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike
summary: Your hit deals an extra 2d6 Radiant damage and the target begins shedding Dim Light in a 5-foot radius. While lit this way it cannot benefit from the Invisible condition, and attack rolls against it have Advantage.
tactics: The only Smite that gives your WHOLE PARTY Advantage, and the only one that is Concentration. THE MATH THAT MAKES IT WORTH IT: Advantage on every attack against the target, from everyone, for up to a minute. Advantage is worth roughly +5 to hit. In a four-person party making eight attacks a round, that is a bigger damage contribution than any Smite in your book — it just shows up on other people's character sheets instead of yours. THE STEALTH ANSWER: 2024 folded hiding into the Invisible condition. Shining Smite explicitly stops a creature from benefiting from Invisible. That makes it a hard counter to invisible stalkers, rogues, shadows, drow using Darkness, and anything that keeps disappearing. If your party has no other answer to hidden enemies, this spell IS the answer. THE COST YOU MUST WEIGH: it is Concentration, so casting it drops Bless, Shield of Faith, or Compelled Duel. Do not cast it reflexively. Cast it when the target is the only thing that matters and the whole party is about to focus fire — a boss, or an invisible enemy you have finally cornered. STAY ALIVE TO KEEP IT: you have to survive in melee while concentrating. Every hit is a Constitution save at DC 10 or half damage. Consider Resilient (Constitution) if this is your plan A. AT LEVEL 15 (SMOLDERING SMITE): if your DM rules Smoldering Smite as applying to all Smite spells, this becomes 2d6 Radiant plus 1d8 unavoidable Fire plus party-wide Advantage. That is the strongest single button the Hearth build has.

name: Warding Bond

components.materialText: a pair of platinum rings worth 50+ GP each, which you and the target must wear

grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 5 - always prepared
summary: A willing creature you touch gains +1 AC, +1 to all saving throws, and Resistance to all damage. While the bond lasts, every time that creature takes damage, YOU take the same amount of damage. The bond breaks if either of you drops to 0 HP, or if you move more than 60 feet apart.
tactics: This is THE Oath of the Hearth spell, mechanically and thematically. 'Guard the hearth' is literally what it does — you take the wound instead of the person you are protecting. HOW THE RESISTANCE MATH ACTUALLY WORKS, AND WHY IT IS GOOD: the target takes HALF damage, and YOU take the amount THEY took after resistance. So a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 10 to you. Total damage to the party is unchanged — but you have MOVED it from a d6-hit-die caster with 30 HP onto a d10 Paladin with heavy armor, Lay on Hands, and a healing pool. That is the entire point: you are not reducing damage, you are relocating it onto the character best equipped to absorb it. COMBINE WITH YOUR AURA OF SOLACE (level 7): you have Resistance to Fire, Cold, and Psychic. Warding Bond damage is damage YOU take — if your DM rules it retains its damage type (most do), your Aura of Solace halves it AGAIN. Warding Bond a caster against a fire-breathing enemy and a 20-point hit becomes 10 to them and 5 to you. That is the strongest defensive combination in the entire Hearth build and your app should surface it explicitly. THE COMPONENT COST YOUR APP MUST TRACK: 100 GP of platinum rings, and they are WORN, not consumed — so you buy them once and reuse them forever. But you must actually own them, a focus cannot substitute, and the target has to be wearing one. Put them in your equipment list now. THE 60-FOOT LEASH IS A TACTICAL CONSTRAINT: the bond breaks if you separate. That means you cannot bond the scout. Bond the person who will stand near you — usually the same person standing in your 10-foot Aura of Protection. Your positioning doctrine and your bonding choice should be the same decision. THE DANGER: it breaks when YOU hit 0. If you are already hurt, bonding someone can kill you both. Check your own HP before casting. Never bond while below half. NO CONCENTRATION, ONE HOUR: it runs alongside Bless or Compelled Duel. This is a huge deal — it is the only major defensive buff you own that does not compete for Concentration. SUBCLASS REDUNDANCY WARNING: your oath grants Warding Bond as an always-prepared spell at Paladin level 5, and it is ALSO on the standard Paladin spell list. Do not spend one of your seven prepared-spell picks on it. Your app must dedupe this or you will silently waste a prepared slot.

name: Zone of Truth
summary: You create a 15-foot-radius Sphere of magic. Each creature that enters or starts its turn there must succeed on a Charisma save or be unable to speak a deliberate lie while inside. You know which creatures succeeded and which failed. Affected creatures are aware of the effect.
tactics: A social-encounter tool with a specific, limited job — and knowing that job is the difference between it being strong and it being a trap. WHAT IT ACTUALLY DOES: it prevents deliberate lies. It does NOT compel answers. A subject who knows they are in the zone can simply refuse to speak, answer a different question, or give a true but useless answer. Enemies always know they are affected. SO USE IT THE OTHER WAY ROUND: the real value is letting an HONEST person PROVE they are honest — clearing a suspected traitor, verifying an ally, confirming a witness. That is a job nothing else does. THE CHANGELING ANGLE, AND THIS IS YOURS SPECIFICALLY: you are a shapeshifter with Advantage on Charisma checks while shifted. You are the party's infiltrator. Zone of Truth constrains what a subject can say but says nothing about who they appear to be — you can be inside your own zone, in a false face, telling the literal truth. Frame your questions so that true answers still serve you. YOU KNOW WHO PASSED THE SAVE: that alone is intelligence. Anyone who succeeds on a Charisma save against a truth spell is either powerful or has something to hide. Watch the ones who pass. PREPARED-LIST VERDICT: swap it in for investigation or negotiation sessions. Do not carry it into a dungeon.

name: Aura of Vitality

healing.note: one creature in the Emanation, automatically when you create the aura and again at the start of each of your turns. NO ACTION COST.

summary: A 30-foot Emanation of healing energy radiates from you for the duration. When you create the aura, and again at the start of each of your turns while it lasts, you can restore 2d6 Hit Points to one creature in it.
tactics: CORRECTION FOR YOUR APP: in 2024 this healing costs NO ACTION. The 2014 version required a Bonus Action each turn; the 2024 version does not - it simply happens when you create the aura and at the start of each of your turns. D&D Beyond's own tooltip is known to still show the stale 2014 wording, so most character tools have this wrong. Getting it right changes the spell from a trap into a strong combat pick. WHY THAT MATTERS SO MUCH: with no action cost, Aura of Vitality is 2d6 of free healing every round while you continue to attack twice AND cast Divine Smite with your Bonus Action. You are healing 7 a round for free. Over ten rounds that is up to 20d6, averaging 70 Hit Points, from one level 3 slot - the same total as the level 6 Heal spell, delivered without ever giving up a turn. THE ONLY REAL COST IS CONCENTRATION. It competes with Bless, Crusader's Mantle, Beacon of Hope and Faerie Fire. Rule of thumb: Aura of Vitality when the party is taking steady chip damage and the fight will run long; Bless when the fight will be short and decided by hit rates. POSITIONING IS THE SKILL: it is a 30-foot Emanation anchored to YOU, so it moves as you move and no action is needed to reposition it. You can heal a downed ally across the room without walking there - compare Lay on Hands, which is Touch. In practice this means you should stand where the largest number of wounded allies fall inside 30 feet, which for a Hearth Paladin is the same place your Aura of Protection wants you anyway. OUT OF COMBAT IT IS STILL THE BEST HEALING IN YOUR BOOK: cast it the moment a fight ends and top off the whole party over ten quiet rounds, saving everyone's Hit Point Dice for the next Short Rest. ONE CREATURE PER TURN. You cannot split the 2d6. Spend it on whoever is closest to dropping.

name: Beacon of Hope
grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 9 - always prepared
summary: Any number of creatures you choose within range gain Advantage on Wisdom saving throws and on Death Saving Throws, and they regain the maximum number of Hit Points possible from any healing they receive, for the duration.
tactics: The most underrated spell your oath grants, and a perfect thematic fit — it is the mechanical form of 'gather to the hearth those in need.' MAXIMUM HEALING IS THE HEADLINE: every healing die rolled for an affected creature is treated as its maximum. Cure Wounds becomes 16 instead of 9. Your ally's Healing Word becomes 4 instead of 2.5. Most importantly, a Cleric's Mass Cure Wounds or Prayer of Healing under Beacon of Hope roughly doubles in value. If your party has a dedicated healer, casting this before they act is the single highest-value thing you can do with an Action. IMPORTANT LIMITATION YOUR APP SHOULD STATE: Lay on Hands is a FLAT number from a pool, not a die roll. Beacon of Hope does not improve it. This spell multiplies your PARTY's healing, not yours. It is a support spell for a party with a healer, not a self-buff. ADVANTAGE ON DEATH SAVES IS A QUIET LIFESAVER: a downed ally under Beacon of Hope is passing death saves roughly 75%% of the time instead of 55%%, and a natural 20 (which brings them back at 1 HP) becomes almost twice as likely. In a fight where people are dropping, this is the spell that stops the cascade. ADVANTAGE ON WISDOM SAVES covers Hold Person, Fear, Command, Dominate Person, Confusion, and most mind-control. Combined with your Aura of Protection's Charisma bonus, an ally in your aura under Beacon of Hope is nearly immune to being turned against the party. IT IS CONCENTRATION AND HAS NO ONGOING RANGE LIMIT — cast it while the party is stacked, then spread. THE DECISION AT LEVEL 9: your Concentration can hold Bless, Faerie Fire, Beacon of Hope, or Aura of Vitality. Beacon of Hope is correct in the attrition fight — long, grinding, people going down. Bless is correct in the fast fight. Faerie Fire is correct in the crowded fight.

name: Blinding Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

save.when: end of each of the target's turns

summary: Your hit deals an extra 3d8 Radiant damage and the target must succeed on a Constitution save or be Blinded for the duration, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns.
tactics: Compared to Divine Smite cast at level 3 (4d8), you give up 1d8 for a chance to Blind. Take that trade almost every time. WHY BLINDED IS WORTH MORE THAN 4.5 DAMAGE: a Blinded creature auto-fails any check requiring sight, has Disadvantage on all its attacks, and grants Advantage on all attacks against it. For a full party that is worth roughly six to eight attack rolls converted per round. Even ONE round of it beats the damage. NOT CONCENTRATION — this is the key advantage over Shining Smite. You can Blind a boss and still be running Bless. TARGET SELECTION: Constitution saves are the enemy's best save, so pick low-Con targets — casters, Fey, most humanoids. Never spend it on a Giant or a Construct. THE BLINDNESS COMBO: a Blinded enemy cannot see you, which means YOUR attacks against it have Advantage and its attacks against you have Disadvantage. Stack that with Shield of Faith and a blinded boss is hitting you roughly one swing in six. SPECIAL TARGETS: anything with a gaze attack, a Medusa, a Beholder, an archer. Blinding an archer removes it from the fight entirely.

name: Create Food and Water
summary: You conjure 45 pounds of plain food and 30 gallons of water, enough to feed fifteen humanoids and give them drink for a day. It spoils after 24 hours if uneaten.
tactics: Mechanically minor, thematically the most Oath-of-the-Hearth spell that exists. 'Gather to the hearth those in need of warmth and rest' is this spell. THE CAMPAIGN-LEVEL PLAY: fifteen people fed per casting. With three level 3 slots you feed forty-five people a day, indefinitely. That is a besieged village, a refugee column, a prison break, a plague quarantine. Combine with Purify Food and Drink and you are the reason a settlement survives a winter. Most tables will give you real narrative leverage — allies, information, safe harbor — for this that no combat spell buys. PREPARED-LIST VERDICT: not a daily pick. Swap it in when the story needs it. Your app should surface it under a 'downtime and narrative' category rather than burying it with combat spells.

name: Crusader's Mantle

damage.note: added to each weapon hit by you and allies in the Emanation

summary: A 30-foot Emanation of divine power radiates from you. You and your allies inside it add 1d4 Radiant damage to every weapon attack that hits.
tactics: Divine Favor for the whole party. Whether it is good depends entirely on one number: how many attacks per round does your party make? DO THE MATH BEFORE YOU PREPARE IT. 1d4 averages 2.5. In a party of four making eight attacks a round, that is 20 extra damage per round for ten rounds — 200 damage from one level 3 slot, and that is enormous. In a party of two melee characters making three attacks a round, it is 7.5 a round and a level 3 Divine Smite (4d8, avg 18) beats it over a short fight. IT LOVES MULTI-ATTACKERS: a Fighter with Action Surge, a Monk with Flurry of Blows, a two-weapon Rogue, a Ranger with Extra Attack. If your party has two or more of those, this is your best level 3 spell. THE 30-FOOT EMANATION IS A POSITIONING PROBLEM: allies must be INSIDE it when they attack. That means your party has to fight as a cluster, which is exactly what your Aura of Protection wants anyway — but it is also exactly what an enemy Fireball wants. Your Aura of Solace gives Fire resistance inside 10 feet, not 30. Be aware of the gap. CONCENTRATION COMPETITION: it fights Bless for the same slot in your head. Rule of thumb — Bless when your party is missing, Crusader's Mantle when your party is hitting but not killing fast enough.

name: Daylight
summary: A 60-foot-radius Sphere of Bright Light appears, with Dim Light for another 60 feet beyond it. You can center it on a point or on an object you hold. If any of the area overlaps magical Darkness created by a spell of level 3 or lower, that Darkness is dispelled.
tactics: The counterspell to Darkness, and against certain enemies that is the whole fight. THE DROW / SHADOW ANSWER: enemies that fight from magical Darkness are effectively Invisible — they get Advantage on attacks and you get Disadvantage. Daylight dispels Darkness of level 3 or lower outright. Cast it and the ambush becomes a normal fight. CAST IT ON AN OBJECT YOU CARRY — this is the trick most people miss. Centering it on your shield or a coin in your pocket means the light MOVES WITH YOU for a full hour with no Concentration. You become a walking 60-foot bright zone. Then put the object in a pouch to switch it off without losing the spell. IT IS NOT SUNLIGHT: it does not trigger sunlight sensitivity or damage vampires. Do not build a plan around that. TACTICAL LIGHTING: Bright Light out to 60 feet means enemies cannot Hide in your zone, and your allies without Darkvision fight at full effect. In a party with humans, that is a real combat buff. HEARTH FLAVOR: a Hearth Paladin carrying a light that cannot be put out is close to perfect thematics — flavor it as your Hearthfire Manifest blazing brighter.

name: Dispel Magic
higherLevel: Automatically ends spells of a level equal to or less than the slot level used.
summary: Choose one creature, object, or magical effect within range. Every spell of level 3 or lower on it ends. For each spell of level 4 or higher, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability against DC 10 + that spell's level; on a success, that spell ends too.
tactics: The universal answer key. It ends walls, domination, invisibility, flight, buffs, barriers — anything that is a spell. THE PARTY QUESTION FIRST: you get level 3 slots at Paladin level 9. Your Wizard or Cleric got them at character level 5 and has more of them. If a full caster in your party has this prepared, do NOT spend one of your precious prepared slots on it. If nobody does, you must. USE IT ON PEOPLE, NOT JUST THINGS: the most valuable Dispel Magic is the one that frees your Dominated Fighter before he kills your Wizard. Have your app remind you that Dispel Magic ends effects on ALLIES, not just enemy buffs. UPCASTING MATH: at level 3 you auto-dispel level 3 and lower and roll for higher. Your check is Charisma-based — at Charisma {CHA} you have +{CHAmod}, so against a level 5 spell you need to beat DC 15. That is a coin flip on your one Action. Upcast when it matters. 120 FEET OF RANGE is enormous for a Paladin. You can strip an enemy's Wall of Force from across the battlefield without leaving your aura.

name: Elemental Weapon

damage.type: chosen: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder

higherLevel: Slot 5-6: +2 attack and 2d4 damage. Slot 7+: +3 attack and 3d4 damage.
summary: A nonmagical weapon you touch gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls and deals an extra 1d4 damage of an elemental type you choose. Requires Concentration.
tactics: Usually the wrong choice, and here is the honest comparison: Magic Weapon (level 2) gives the same +1 to hit for a lower slot, for an hour, with NO Concentration. Elemental Weapon adds 1d4 damage and takes your Concentration — which means giving up Bless. THE BETTER LINE: cast Magic Weapon (level 2, no Concentration) AND Divine Favor (level 1, no Concentration) on separate turns. You end up with +1 to hit and +1d4 damage, identical to Elemental Weapon, and your Concentration is still free for Bless. Elemental Weapon is strictly worse unless you specifically need the damage TYPE. WHEN THE TYPE MATTERS: an enemy resistant to Bludgeoning/Piercing/Slashing but not to Cold. A Troll (fire or acid stops regeneration). Something immune to Radiant, which shuts down your Divine Smite and your Radiant Strikes at level 11. HEARTH BUILD NOTE: choosing Fire makes it thematically perfect and mechanically risky — Fire is the most-resisted type in the game. Your subclass already gives you a lot of Fire. Choosing COLD or LIGHTNING here diversifies your damage profile, which is what a smart build actually wants.

name: Fireball

components.materialText: a ball of bat guano and sulfur

grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 9 - always prepared
summary: A bright streak flashes to a point within range and blossoms into a 20-foot-radius Sphere of flame. Each creature in the Sphere takes 8d6 Fire damage, or half as much on a successful Dexterity save. It ignites flammable objects in the area that no one is holding or wearing.
tactics: A Paladin with Fireball is not a normal Paladin. This is the biggest single thing Oath of the Hearth gives you and it arrives at level 9. 8d6 AVERAGES 28 DAMAGE TO EVERYTHING IN A 20-FOOT SPHERE AT 150 FEET. For comparison, your entire Attack action at level 9 does roughly 25 to one creature. Against two or more enemies Fireball is simply better than fighting, and against five it is four times better. IT DOES NOT EXCLUDE ALLIES — this is the critical difference from Destructive Wave, and the thing that will get a party member killed if your app does not warn about it. Fireball hits everything in the sphere including your friends. You must place it with care. THE 150-FOOT RANGE IS THE WHOLE TACTIC: unlike Burning Hands, you do not have to be in the blast. Hang back on round one, drop Fireball on the enemy cluster before your melee engages, THEN charge in. Sequencing matters — Fireball first, engage second. A Paladin who charges and then wants to Fireball has already made the spell unusable. COORDINATE WITH YOUR PARTY OUT LOUD. Tell your melee 'hold one round, I am opening with Fireball.' The single biggest reason Fireball underperforms at real tables is that the front line already ran in. IT IGNITES OBJECTS: torch a supply wagon, a bridge, a barricade, a ship's rigging, a field. Denying terrain is often worth more than the damage. FIRE RESISTANCE AND IMMUNITY ARE COMMON AT THE LEVELS YOU GET THIS. Devils, fire giants, red dragons, salamanders, most demons. At level 9 you have three level 3 slots — do not spend all of them on a spell the enemy is immune to. Scout first with Divine Sense or Detect Evil and Good. AT LEVEL 13 UPCAST IT WITH YOUR LEVEL 4 SLOT for 9d6. At level 17 a level 5 slot gives 10d6. SLOT ECONOMY WARNING: casting Fireball uses your one spell slot for the turn, so no Smite that round. Fireball rounds and Smite rounds are different rounds. Plan which is which before initiative.

name: Magic Circle

components.materialText: salt and powdered silver worth 100+ GP, which the spell consumes

summary: You create a 10-foot-radius, 20-foot-tall cylinder of magical energy. Choose one or more of Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends, or Undead. Chosen creature types cannot willingly enter the cylinder except on a successful Charisma save, cannot Charm or Frighten anyone inside it, and attack rolls against creatures inside it have Disadvantage. You can invert it to trap those types inside.
tactics: New to the Paladin list in 2024 — it was not a Paladin spell in 2014. Track this in your app, because older sources will not list it. TWO COMPLETELY DIFFERENT USES: outward-facing it is a fortress, inward-facing it is a cage. The cage mode is what makes it worth 100 GP. THE SUMMONING-CONTAINMENT PLAY: cast it inverted, then have your party lure or teleport a Fiend inside. It cannot leave. You now negotiate with a demon from perfect safety, or you kill it at leisure. This is the classic use and it is very strong. THE LAST-STAND PLAY, WHICH IS YOURS: outward-facing, everything of the chosen type attacks you at Disadvantage and cannot Charm or Frighten anyone inside. A 10-foot radius happens to be exactly the size of your Aura of Protection. Stand at the center: allies inside get your Charisma bonus to saves, your Aura of Solace resistances, AND Disadvantage on all attacks against them. That is the single most defensible 20-foot cylinder a level 9 character can create. Hold a doorway with it. THE COSTS ARE REAL: one full minute to cast (you must take the Magic action every turn and maintain Concentration during the casting), and 100 GP of consumed materials every time. This is a spell you cast BEFORE the fight, deliberately, on ground you chose. Your app must track the silver as a consumable and must not let a Spellcasting Focus substitute for it.

name: Remove Curse
summary: Your touch ends all curses affecting one creature or object. For a cursed magic item, the curse remains on the item but attunement to it ends, so it can be discarded or removed.
tactics: Situational and irreplaceable — the two words that together mean 'prepare it the day after you need it, not before.' You can change one prepared spell on every Long Rest. Curses almost never need to be removed inside six seconds. THE ATTUNEMENT CLAUSE IS THE PRACTICAL USE: a cursed item that will not come off your Fighter's hand gets released by this. The item stays cursed; your ally stops being attached to it. LYCANTHROPY AND SIMILAR: many campaign curses — lycanthropy, mummy rot's curse component, a hag's bargain — are removable with this. Ask your DM what tier of curse it handles in their game; some require Greater Restoration or a quest instead. PARTY CHECK: Clerics, Warlocks, Wizards, Bards and Druids all get this. Do not double up.

name: Revivify

components.materialText: a diamond worth 300+ GP, which the spell consumes

summary: You touch a creature that has died within the last minute and it returns to life with 1 Hit Point. It cannot restore missing body parts and does not work on a creature that died of old age.
