tactics: If you can prepare this, prepare it. Every session. There is no argument. THE ONE-MINUTE WINDOW IS THE WHOLE SPELL: ten rounds. That is generous in combat and brutally short afterward. The moment an ally dies, a clock starts. Everyone at the table should know who is carrying Revivify and where the diamond is. BUY THE DIAMOND NOW AND BUY TWO. 300 GP, consumed on cast. A party that does not own a diamond in advance loses a character permanently to a bad round. Your app should treat 'Revivify diamond in inventory' as a hard readiness check and warn when it is missing. A Spellcasting Focus cannot substitute — it is a costed, consumed component. THEY COME BACK AT 1 HP: which means they will drop again to the next hit. Plan the follow-up before you cast — Lay on Hands as your next Bonus Action, or have someone drag them out. Reviving someone into the same area of effect that killed them is a wasted diamond. STACK IT WITH GENTLE REPOSE: if you are past the one-minute window, ritual-cast Gentle Repose to pause the ten-day Raise Dead clock. Between the two spells, death at your table becomes a logistics problem instead of a permanent loss. That is the Hearth oath doing its job.

name: Aura of Life
summary: A 30-foot Emanation of life-preserving energy radiates from you. You and your allies inside it have Resistance to Necrotic damage, and your Hit Point maximums cannot be reduced. In addition, an ally in the aura that has 0 Hit Points regains 1 Hit Point at the start of its turn.
tactics: The anti-undead aura, and the only spell in your book that automatically picks allies back up off the floor. THE AUTO-REVIVE CLAUSE IS THE REAL SPELL: an ally at 0 HP inside the aura stands back up at 1 HP at the start of its turn, every turn, with no action from anyone. Against enemies that do not multi-attack a downed character, that makes your party effectively unkillable while you concentrate. It also means nobody is rolling Death Saves. THE HP-MAXIMUM CLAUSE MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: wights, wraiths, spectres and many undead reduce Hit Point maximum permanently until a Long Rest. That damage is not healable. Aura of Life blocks it entirely. In an undead campaign this is the difference between attrition and a war of position. TEN MINUTES, 30 FEET: cast it before you open the crypt door, not after. Ten minutes is long enough to cover a whole dungeon room. CONCENTRATION COST: it competes with Bless, Aura of Purity, and Compelled Duel. Aura of Life is the right pick specifically against Necrotic and undead; Aura of Purity is the better general-purpose aura. Prepare both if you can; concentrate on the one that matches the enemy. HEARTH SYNERGY: you already give Fire, Cold and Psychic resistance in your 10-foot aura. Aura of Life adds Necrotic at 30 feet. Together you are covering five damage types across two overlapping zones.

name: Aura of Purity
summary: A 30-foot Emanation radiates from you. You and your allies inside it have Resistance to Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against becoming Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned.
tactics: The broadest defensive spell a Paladin ever gets, and probably the best level 4 slot you will spend. COUNT THE CONDITIONS: seven of the fifteen conditions in the game, covered by Advantage, for everyone within 30 feet, for ten minutes. Paralyzed and Stunned alone are the two conditions most likely to kill a party member outright — a Paralyzed ally takes automatic critical hits from anything within 5 feet. STACK IT WITH YOUR AURA OF PROTECTION AND THIS BECOMES ABSURD: your Aura of Protection already gives everyone within 10 feet +Charisma to saves. Add Aura of Purity's Advantage on those same saves. At Charisma {CHA} that is Advantage plus +{CHAmod} — a party member who was making a DC 15 Hold Person save about half the time is now making it most of the time. You have functionally deleted save-or-suck effects from the encounter. THE TWO AURAS HAVE DIFFERENT RADII — TEACH YOUR PARTY THIS: Aura of Protection is 10 feet (30 at level 18), Aura of Purity is 30. Allies at 25 feet get the Advantage but not the bonus. If you want the full stack, they must be inside 10 feet of you. Your positioning instruction to the party is literally 'stand within ten feet of me.' THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: clustering the party within 10 feet is exactly what an enemy area-of-effect wants. Your Aura of Solace covers Fire, Cold and Psychic within 10 feet, so most common blasts are already halved for anyone standing in the tight formation. That is the Hearth build's whole thesis: cluster up, and make clustering safe. PREPARE THIS OVER AURA OF LIFE unless you know you are fighting undead.

name: Banishment
higherLevel: Target one additional creature per slot level above 4.
summary: One creature you can see must succeed on a Charisma save or be transported to a harmless demiplane for the duration, incapacitated and unable to act. If the target is native to a different plane of existence and the spell lasts the full minute, it is banished permanently and does not return.
tactics: The single most powerful thing a Paladin can do with one Action. It removes an enemy from the fight entirely — no damage race, no attrition, just gone. CHARISMA SAVES ARE THE WEAKNESS OF ALMOST EVERYTHING: Beasts, Constructs, Giants, Monstrosities, Oozes and most Undead have terrible Charisma saves well into high CR. Even a Paladin with middling Charisma lands this. Check the target's Charisma before you commit — it is the one number that decides the spell. THE PERMANENT-BANISHMENT CLAUSE IS THE REAL PRIZE: if the target is not native to your plane and you hold Concentration the full minute, it never comes back. Against a summoned demon, an elemental, or an invading celestial, Banishment is not a delay — it is a kill. That is worth defending your Concentration for ten rounds with everything you have. THE SPLIT-THE-FIGHT PLAY: in a two-boss encounter, banish one and fight the other four-on-one. Your party wins that trade decisively. This is the correct opener against any encounter with two serious threats — do not save it for when you are losing. PROTECT YOUR CONCENTRATION AFTER YOU CAST: banish the enemy, then immediately reposition somewhere you will take the fewest separate hits. Each hit is a separate Concentration save. Going Prone behind cover is not beneath you here. DO NOT DROP IT FOR BANISHING SMITE AT LEVEL 17 — Banishing Smite requires the target to already be below 50 HP and still allows a save. Banishment works at full health.

name: Death Ward
summary: You touch a creature and ward it against death. The first time it would drop to 0 Hit Points during the duration, it drops to 1 Hit Point instead. If an effect would kill it outright without dealing damage, that effect fails. The spell then ends.
tactics: Eight hours, no Concentration, and it cancels one death. Cast it at breakfast and forget about it. THE MORNING ROUTINE: at level 13+ your day should start with Aid on the party and Death Ward on whoever is most likely to die. Both are long-duration, neither takes Concentration, both are cast safely before you leave camp. A Paladin who does this is playing a different game from one who does not. IT ALSO STOPS INSTANT-DEATH EFFECTS: Power Word Kill, a Disintegrate that would reduce to 0, a Banshee's wail, Finger of Death. Those are the effects that end characters permanently with no death saves. Death Ward is the only pre-emptive answer you have. WHO TO PUT IT ON: not you. You have the most hit points, the best armor, Lay on Hands, and an aura. Put it on the Wizard, the Rogue, or whoever the DM keeps targeting. If you truly cannot pick, put it on whoever is carrying the party's Revivify diamond. IT DOES NOT STACK OR REFRESH: it ends when it triggers. Recast the next morning. Your app should track the eight-hour timer and whether it has already fired.

name: Fire Shield

components.materialText: a bit of phosphorus or a firefly

damage.type: Fire or Cold (matching the shield you chose)
damage.note: to a creature that hits you with a melee attack while within 5 feet

grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 13 - always prepared
summary: Flames wreathe your body for 10 minutes, shedding Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for another 10 feet. You choose a warm shield, which gives you Resistance to Cold damage, or a chill shield, which gives you Resistance to Fire damage. Whenever a creature within 5 feet hits you with a melee attack, it takes 2d8 damage of the shield's type. No Concentration.
tactics: Ten minutes, no Concentration, and it punishes everything that touches you. For a front-line Paladin this is close to a free upgrade. NO CONCENTRATION IS THE ENTIRE REASON THIS IS GOOD: at level 13 you can be running Aura of Purity or Banishment on your Concentration AND wearing Fire Shield at the same time. Almost nothing else in your book stacks like this. Cast it before the fight and forget it. PICK THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT YOU ALREADY HAVE. This is the key decision and most people get it backwards. Your Aura of Solace at level 7 already gives you Resistance to Fire AND Cold. So the resistance half of Fire Shield is redundant for you — choose based on the DAMAGE TYPE you want to deal instead. Choose the CHILL shield (which deals Cold) when fighting fire-immune enemies like devils and fire elementals, because your entire Hearth kit is Fire and those enemies otherwise wall you out. Choose the WARM shield (Fire) for thematics and against cold-vulnerable enemies. Your app should surface this reversal — picking for the damage type rather than the resistance is the Hearth-specific insight. STACK IT WITH HEARTHFIRE MANIFEST: your level 3 Channel Divinity cloak already deals 1d10 Fire when you are hit by a melee attack. Fire Shield adds 2d8. Together that is roughly 14 damage to every enemy that hits you in melee, on top of whatever your weapons are doing. Against a swarm of attackers you become an area-damage effect that fights back automatically. That combination is the level 13 Hearth power spike and your app should present it as a named combo. IT LIGHTS YOU UP — literally. Bright Light in 10 feet means you cannot hide, and enemies can see you from far away. This is a spell for the character who WANTS to be seen and charged, which is exactly the Hearth role. But if the party is sneaking, do not cast it. THE DAMAGE IS AUTOMATIC AND HAS NO SAVE AND NO LIMIT ON USES. Every melee hit, every round, for ten minutes.

name: Locate Creature

components.materialText: a bit of fur from a bloodhound

summary: You sense the direction to a creature you name or describe, or to the nearest creature of a specific kind, as long as it is within 1,000 feet. Running water at least 10 feet wide blocks the sense, and it fails if the target has changed form.
tactics: A tracking spell that is better than any mundane Survival check and worse than most people expect. THE 1,000-FOOT LIMIT IS THE PROBLEM: that is about 200 feet of movement per round for a fleeing target on a fast mount. If your quarry is running and you are not faster, you will lose the sense. Use it mounted — a Warhorse from Find Steed moves 60 feet a round and closes the gap. THE SHAPESHIFTER CLAUSE, AND THIS ONE IS PERSONAL: the spell fails if the target has changed form. You are a Changeling. Locate Creature does not find you while you are shifted. Remember that when an enemy is hunting your party — you are the one member they cannot magically track. Use it. RUNNING WATER BLOCKS IT: if you are being tracked this way, cross a stream. GENERIC-TYPE MODE IS UNDERUSED: 'the nearest Fiend' or 'the nearest Undead' turns a dungeon into a map. Combine with Divine Sense at 60 feet for a two-tier detection net. PREPARED-LIST VERDICT: swap in when the session is a hunt. Not a standing pick.

name: Staggering Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike
summary: Your hit deals an extra 4d6 Psychic damage and the target must succeed on a Wisdom save or have the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn.
tactics: Stunned is the strongest condition in the game that is not death, and this is the only way a Paladin applies it. WHAT STUNNED ACTUALLY DOES: the target is Incapacitated (no action, no bonus action, no reaction, and in 2024 it also LOSES CONCENTRATION and cannot speak), it auto-fails all Strength and Dexterity saves, and every attack against it has Advantage. For one full round the enemy simply does not play. THE CONCENTRATION-BREAK IS NEW AND HUGE: in 2024, Incapacitated explicitly ends Concentration. Stunning an enemy caster strips their Wall of Force, their Hold Person, their Haste — automatically, with no damage-based save. That alone is worth a level 4 slot. THE FOLLOW-UP IS WHERE THE FIGHT IS WON: a Stunned target auto-fails Strength and Dexterity saves. Tell your party BEFORE you cast — the wizard should have a Dexterity-save spell ready, the rogue should be positioned for Advantage. A stun that nobody capitalizes on is a wasted slot. PSYCHIC IS EXCELLENT: almost nothing resists it, and it is one of the few damage types that gets past the Fire-immune enemies your Hearth kit otherwise struggles with. TARGET SELECTION: Wisdom save, so avoid Clerics, Fey and Aberrations. Brutes, Beasts and Constructs usually fail. TIMING: like all Smites you cast it after the hit lands. On a critical hit, the 4d6 doubles to 8d6 — and a big Psychic crit into a stun is usually the round a boss fight turns.

name: Wall of Fire
grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 13 - always prepared
summary: You create a wall of fire on a solid surface: either a straight wall up to 60 feet long, 20 feet high and 1 foot thick, or a ringed wall up to 20 feet in diameter and 20 feet high. It is opaque. When it appears, each creature in its area makes a Dexterity save, taking 5d8 Fire damage on a failure or half on a success. One side of the wall, chosen when you cast it, deals 5d8 Fire damage to any creature that ends its turn within 10 feet of that side or inside the wall.
tactics: This is the Oath of the Hearth capstone spell in everything but name: you are literally creating a hearth on the battlefield and deciding who is inside it. IT IS A CONTROL SPELL, NOT A DAMAGE SPELL. The initial burst is fine. The value is that a 60-foot opaque wall cuts the battlefield in half and enemies must either walk through it, walk around it, or stop. Any of those three is a win. THE ONE-SIDED DAMAGE IS THE CRAFT: only one side burns creatures that end their turn near it. Choose the enemy side. Now your party can stand safely at the wall's edge while the enemy cannot approach without taking 5d8 every round. You have created a kill zone that costs you nothing to maintain. THE RING FORM IS THE HEARTH: a 20-foot-diameter ring, 20 feet high, with the damaging side facing OUTWARD. Your party stands inside. Anything that wants to reach you takes 5d8 to enter and 5d8 every round it stays near. Combine with your Aura of Protection and Aura of Solace inside the ring and you have built the most defensible 20 feet on the map. This is the play your entire subclass points at — make sure your app surfaces the ring option, because most tools only show the straight-wall version. IT IS OPAQUE — that matters as much as the damage. It blocks line of sight, which blocks most enemy spells (they need to see the target), blocks archers, and lets your party disengage or heal unseen. SPLIT THE ENEMY FORCE: drop the wall through the middle of an enemy formation. Now you are fighting half an army and the other half is on the wrong side. This is the highest-leverage use in any fight with more than four enemies. CONCENTRATION AT LEVEL 13 competes with Aura of Purity and Banishment. Wall of Fire is right when the problem is NUMBERS or POSITION; the auras are right when the problem is enemy magic. FIRE-IMMUNE ENEMIES WALK THROUGH IT UNHARMED — but it is still opaque and still blocks line of sight. It never becomes useless, only less lethal.

name: Banishing Smite
castingTime: Bonus Action, taken immediately after hitting a creature with a Melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike
summary: Your hit deals an extra 5d10 Force damage. If that damage leaves the target with 50 Hit Points or fewer, it must succeed on a Charisma save or be banished to a harmless demiplane for the duration, incapacitated. If the spell ends while it is still there, it reappears where it was.
tactics: Big damage with a conditional finisher attached, and the condition is why it is not as good as it sounds. 5d10 FORCE (avg 27.5) IS THE REAL VALUE: Force is resisted by almost nothing in the game. As raw damage this beats a level 5 Divine Smite (6d8, avg 27) by a hair and is far less likely to be halved. THE BANISHMENT RIDER IS UNRELIABLE: the target must be at 50 HP or fewer AFTER the damage, and then it still gets a Charisma save. Against anything worth banishing, it will usually be above 50 HP. Treat the banishment as a bonus, never as the plan. BANISHMENT (LEVEL 4) IS THE BETTER SPELL for actually removing an enemy — it works at full health and costs a lower slot. Keep both prepared; use Banishment to delete a threat, Banishing Smite to finish one. IT IS CONCENTRATION, WHICH IS A REAL COST: casting it drops Bless, Aura of Purity, or Banishment. If you are already concentrating on something good, just cast Divine Smite at level 5 instead — nearly the same damage, no Concentration. Your app should warn when casting a Concentration Smite would drop an active Concentration spell. THE CLEAN-UP USE: an enemy at low HP that your party cannot finish this round, that is about to flee or heal. Banish it, kill the rest, then let it return alone into a full party.

name: Circle of Power
summary: A 30-foot Emanation of protective energy radiates from you. You and your allies inside it have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. In addition, when an affected creature succeeds on a save that would normally deal half damage on a success, it takes no damage instead.
tactics: The anti-caster aura, and against high-level spellcasting enemies it is the strongest defensive spell in the entire Paladin list. THE 'NO DAMAGE ON A SUCCESSFUL SAVE' CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE SPELL: this is Evasion, granted to your entire party, against every spell. An enemy Fireball that would deal 28 to a party of four deals ZERO to everyone who saves. That is not damage reduction, that is negation. STACK THE THREE LAYERS AND DO THE MATH: Aura of Protection (+Charisma to saves, 10 feet) + Circle of Power (Advantage on saves vs magic, 30 feet) + no-damage-on-success. At level 17 with Charisma 20, a party member inside 10 feet of you rolls a Dexterity save against Fireball with Advantage and +5. Against a DC 17 save that is roughly an 80%% success rate, and every success is zero damage. You have made your party immune to enemy blasting. IT IS SAVES AGAINST MAGIC ONLY: a dragon's breath weapon is not a spell in most rulings but IS a magical effect — check with your DM, because that ruling decides whether this spell is good in a dragon fight. CONCENTRATION AT LEVEL 17 IS A HARD CHOICE: Circle of Power competes with Aura of Purity, Banishment, and Holy Weapon. The rule: Circle of Power when the enemy is a caster, Aura of Purity when the enemy applies conditions, Banishment when there is one thing that must go away.

name: Destructive Wave

damage.dice: 5d6 Thunder plus 5d6 Radiant or Necrotic (your choice)

summary: Divine energy erupts from you in a 30-foot Emanation. Each creature you choose in the area must succeed on a Constitution save or take 5d6 Thunder damage plus 5d6 Radiant or Necrotic damage (you choose the second type) and be knocked Prone. On a success it takes half damage and is not knocked Prone.
tactics: The only true area attack a Paladin ever gets, and it solves the class's single biggest structural weakness: crowds. 'EACH CREATURE YOU CHOOSE' IS THE MOST IMPORTANT PHRASE — you exclude your allies automatically. You can stand in the middle of a melee scrum with your entire party and detonate without hurting a single friend. That makes it strictly better than a Fireball for a front-line character. 10d6 AVERAGES 35 DAMAGE TO EVERY ENEMY IN 30 FEET. Against six goblins that is 210 points of damage from one Action. Against one boss it is worse than a Smite. Count heads before you cast: three or more enemies and this is your best level 5 slot; one or two and it is not. THE PRONE RIDER IS THE TACTICAL PAYLOAD: every enemy that fails is knocked Prone. Prone means Disadvantage on their attacks, Advantage for all your melee, and half their movement spent standing. Detonating this and then having your party's melee clean up is a round where the enemy barely acts. TWO DAMAGE TYPES IS DELIBERATE DESIGN: Thunder plus your choice of Radiant or Necrotic. Almost nothing resists all three. Pick Radiant against Undead and Fiends, Necrotic against Celestials and anything Radiant-immune. This is the answer to a Fire-immune enemy that your Hearth kit otherwise cannot hurt. POSITIONING IS THE SKILL: you have to be at the center. Walk INTO the crowd, then detonate. Your heavy armor, Aura of Protection and Aura of Solace exist precisely so you can survive being surrounded. This is the play your whole chassis is built for.

name: Dispel Evil and Good
summary: Shimmering energy surrounds you. Aberrations, Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends and Undead have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you. You can also end the spell early to use one of two effects: Break Enchantment, ending a Charm, Fright or possession on a creature you touch; or Dismissal, forcing a creature of one of those types you touch to make a Charisma save or be sent back to its home plane.
tactics: Three spells in one, and the third is the one that matters. THE BASE EFFECT is Protection from Evil and Good for yourself only, at a level 5 slot instead of a level 1. On its own that is a bad trade — prepare Protection from Evil and Good instead if that is all you want. DISMISSAL IS WHY THIS SPELL EXISTS: creatures banished by Dismissal are sent to their home plane and must return by normal means. That is not a one-minute timeout — that is permanent removal, and unlike Banishment it does not require you to hold Concentration for the full minute. Touch the demon, it fails a Charisma save, it is gone from the campaign. THE LIMIT: Dismissal does nothing to a creature already on its home plane. In the Abyss, this spell does not banish demons. Banishment (level 4) works on natives; Dismissal does not. Carry both and know which situation you are in. BREAK ENCHANTMENT IS THE EMERGENCY BUTTON: ending a Charm, Fright or possession on an ally by touch, with no save, no check, and no chance of failure. When your Fighter is being ridden by a ghost and swinging at the party, this is the answer. TOUCH RANGE MEANS YOU HAVE TO GET THERE. Plan movement first. Mounted, or with Misty Step from Fey-Touched, this becomes reliable.

name: Flame Strike
higherLevel: +1d6 to either the Fire or Radiant damage per slot level above 5.
grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 17 - always prepared
summary: A vertical column of divine fire roars down in a 10-foot-radius, 40-foot-high Cylinder centered on a point you can see. Each creature in it takes 5d6 Fire damage plus 5d6 Radiant damage, or half as much on a successful Dexterity save.
tactics: The perfect thesis spell for Oath of the Hearth: half fire, half divine light, one pillar. TWO DAMAGE TYPES IS THE POINT, NOT THE TOTAL. 10d6 averages 35, which is respectable but not extraordinary at level 17. What makes Flame Strike better than Fireball for you is that only half of it is Fire. Against a fire-resistant enemy, Fireball loses half its damage; Flame Strike loses only a quarter. Against a fire-IMMUNE enemy, Fireball does nothing and Flame Strike still does full Radiant. This is your answer to the devils and fire giants that shut down the rest of your kit. Keep that distinction front and center in your app — it is the single most useful thing to know about this spell. THE SHAPE IS NARROW AND TALL: 10-foot radius, 40 feet high. That is a smaller footprint than Fireball's 20-foot sphere, so it catches fewer enemies — but the 40-foot height means it hits FLYING targets in the column, which Fireball placed at ground level does not. Against airborne enemies stacked above a ground force, Flame Strike hits both layers at once. IT DOES NOT EXCLUDE ALLIES. Same warning as Fireball — place it carefully, and tell your melee before you cast. SLOT SCARCITY IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT: at level 17 you have exactly one level 5 slot. Spending it on Flame Strike means not casting Destructive Wave, Circle of Power, or a level 5 Divine Smite that turn. Flame Strike wins when enemies are clustered AND fire-resistant AND you cannot safely stand in the middle of them; Destructive Wave wins when you can (it excludes allies and knocks targets Prone). AT LEVEL 20 WITH HEARTH WARDEN'S SWIFT FLAME, this becomes castable as a Bonus Action — meaning Flame Strike plus a full Attack action in one turn. That is the payoff of the capstone.

name: Geas

damage.note: each day the target acts contrary to the command, once per day

summary: You place a magical command on a creature that can understand you. On a failed Wisdom save it is Charmed by you and must follow your command to the best of its ability for 30 days. Each day it acts in a way directly counter to your instructions, it takes 5d10 Psychic damage, once per day. A command that is obviously self-destructive ends the spell.
tactics: A one-minute casting time with a Verbal component means this is never a combat spell. It is a downtime, interrogation, and campaign-politics tool — and used well it is enormously powerful. THE PROCEDURE: subdue and restrain the target first. Then spend a full minute chanting (you must take the Magic action every turn and maintain Concentration during the casting; if interrupted the spell fails but you keep the slot). Then give the command. WRITE THE COMMAND CAREFULLY — this is the whole skill. Vague commands get lawyered. Self-destructive commands end the spell instantly. The best commands are specific, verifiable, and consume the target's time: 'Travel to the city of X and remain there peacefully for thirty days' neutralizes an enemy commander for a month without killing them. THE CHARMED CONDITION IS A HIDDEN BONUS: a Charmed creature gives YOU Advantage on social ability checks against it. A Geased subject is easier to persuade about everything, not just the command. Over thirty days that turns an enemy into an asset. THE DAMAGE DOES NOT SCALE, AND THAT IS THE FLAW: 5d10 averages 27 and never increases. A high-level target can simply eat the damage once a day, take a Short Rest, and ignore you. Against anything with serious hit points, Geas is a leash made of thread. Use it on people, not monsters. HEARTH FRAMING: a Paladin who binds enemies instead of killing them is playing the oath, not just the class. Geas is how you take a prisoner who stays taken.

name: Greater Restoration

components.materialText: diamond dust worth 100+ GP, which the spell consumes

summary: Your touch removes one of the following from a creature: one level of Exhaustion, one effect Charming or Petrifying it, one curse (including attunement to a cursed item), any reduction to one of its ability scores, or any effect reducing its Hit Point maximum.
tactics: The universal repair spell. Most of what it fixes cannot be fixed any other way. EXHAUSTION IS THE MOST COMMON USE, AND 2024 MADE IT MATTER MORE: exhaustion is now a flat -2 penalty to every d20 Test per level and -5 feet of Speed per level, cumulative to six levels where the creature dies. A character at three levels of exhaustion is at -6 to everything. Only a Long Rest (one level) or this spell removes it. In a forced-march, plague, or death-and-revival scenario, Greater Restoration is the only thing keeping the party functional. HP MAXIMUM REDUCTION: wights, wraiths and similar undead permanently lower Hit Point maximums. This is the cure. Aura of Life prevents it; Greater Restoration repairs it after the fact. PETRIFIED: a petrified ally is a statue and does nothing until this is cast. There is no other practical answer at your level. BUY THE DIAMOND DUST IN ADVANCE — 100 GP, consumed, no focus substitution. Along with the Revivify diamond, this is one of two consumables that should never be missing from a Paladin's pack. Your app should treat both as hard readiness checks. PARTY CHECK: Bards, Clerics and Druids get this too. If one of them carries it, spend your one level 5 slot on Destructive Wave or Circle of Power instead — but confirm before you assume.

name: Hallow

components.materialText: incense worth 1,000+ GP, which the spell consumes

grantedBy: Oath of the Hearth, Paladin level 17 - always prepared
summary: You touch a point and infuse the area around it (up to a 60-foot radius) with holy power. Celestials, Elementals, Fey, Fiends and Undead cannot willingly enter the area, and creatures in it cannot be Charmed, Frightened or possessed by those creature types. You then bind one additional effect to the area from a list including Courage, Darkness, Daylight, Energy Protection, Energy Vulnerability, Everlasting Rest, Extradimensional Interference, Fear, Silence and Tongues, and you choose whether it applies to everyone or only to a designated group.
tactics: Not a combat spell in any sense — 24 hours to cast and 1,000 GP consumed. It is a CAMPAIGN spell, and for an Oath of the Hearth Paladin it may be the most on-theme thing in the entire game: you are making a permanent sanctuary. Literally building a hearth that never goes out. IT LASTS UNTIL DISPELLED. Permanent. One casting, one thousand gold, and a place on the map is forever warded. Over a campaign that is an enormous return. THE SECOND EFFECT IS WHERE THE POWER IS, AND ENERGY PROTECTION IS USUALLY THE PICK: choose a damage type and everyone in the 60-foot radius has Resistance to it. Hallow your party's stronghold with Energy Protection (Fire) and you have made the place siege-proof against dragon breath. THE 'DESIGNATED GROUP' CLAUSE IS THE TACTICAL CORE: you choose who the second effect applies to. So you can Hallow a battlefield chokepoint with FEAR applied to everyone EXCEPT your allies, or COURAGE applied only to your side. A prepared defensive position with Hallow on it is a fight you have already won before it starts. EXTRADIMENSIONAL INTERFERENCE blocks teleportation into the area — that is how you stop an enemy wizard from bypassing your defenses, and how you keep a rescued group safe from being snatched. EVERLASTING REST stops the dead in the area from rising. In an undead campaign, hallowing a graveyard is a permanent solution to a recurring problem. PLAN IT WITH YOUR DM. 24 hours of uninterrupted casting means you need a safe location and downtime. This is a spell you tell the DM you intend to cast a session in advance so they can build around it. Do not expect to improvise it. APP NOTE: this should live in a downtime/narrative category, not the combat spell list, and it should carry a hard 1,000 GP consumable check.

name: Raise Dead

components.materialText: a diamond worth 500+ GP, which the spell consumes

summary: You return a creature that has been dead for no more than 10 days to life with 1 Hit Point. It cannot restore missing body parts and does not work on Undead or Constructs. The creature takes a -4 penalty to all D20 Tests, which reduces by 1 each time it finishes a Long Rest until the penalty is gone.
tactics: Your safety net for when Revivify's one-minute window closed. STACK IT WITH GENTLE REPOSE — THIS IS THE COMPLETE DEATH PROTOCOL for an Oath of the Hearth Paladin: (1) ally dies; (2) if within 1 minute, Revivify (level 3, 300 GP diamond); (3) if not, ritual-cast Gentle Repose (level 2, free, 10 minutes) which pauses the 10-day clock indefinitely; (4) get to a safe place and cast Raise Dead (level 5, 1 hour, 500 GP diamond). Between those three spells, death at your table stops being permanent and becomes a logistics problem. That protocol IS your oath. THE -4 PENALTY IS SEVERE AND SHOULD DRIVE PACING: a raised character is at -4 to every attack, check and save for four Long Rests. They are not combat-effective. Do not raise someone and immediately walk into the boss fight — rest first, or accept that you are fighting a man down. ONE HOUR CASTING TIME: you must take the Magic action every turn for the full hour and maintain Concentration. This is a safe-camp spell. Never attempt it in hostile territory. 500 GP CONSUMED. Track it. A party that does not budget for resurrection diamonds is a party that loses characters permanently, and your app should have a persistent readiness widget for it.

name: Summon Celestial
higherLevel: The spirit's Armor Class, Hit Points, and attack damage increase with the slot level.
summary: You summon a Celestial spirit in one of two forms: Avenger (a ranged attacker with a radiant bow) or Defender (a melee protector that can absorb damage aimed at allies). It acts on your initiative, obeys your verbal commands, and takes its turn immediately after yours. Its attack bonus uses your spell attack modifier.
tactics: An extra body on the field, and bodies are worth more than damage. IT DOES NOT COST YOU AN ACTION AFTER TURN ONE: you spend one Action to summon, then it attacks every round for an hour while you also attack. That is a permanent doubling of your action economy for one slot. Action economy, not damage, is what wins fights in 5.5e. PICK DEFENDER, NOT AVENGER, AS A HEARTH PALADIN: the Defender form can take damage aimed at an ally within 5 feet of it. That is a second Warding Bond that walks around on its own. Station the Defender next to your Wizard while you hold the front — now you are protecting two positions at once, which no other level 5 spell lets you do. THE ATTACK BONUS WARNING: the summon uses YOUR spell attack modifier, which is Charisma-based. If your Charisma is 18 your spell attack is +7 at level 17 — noticeably worse than a martial's. The Avenger's damage looks good on paper and misses a lot. This is the main reason to take Defender. IT BLOCKS SPACE AND MAKES OPPORTUNITY ATTACKS: even ignoring its damage, a body in a corridor is a wall. Use it to hold a second doorway, to cut off a flanking route, or to stand on the downed ally you cannot reach. THE 500 GP RELIQUARY IS NOT CONSUMED — buy it once, keep it forever. But you must own it and a focus cannot substitute. Add it to your permanent equipment list. CONCENTRATION: it competes with Circle of Power and Aura of Purity. Summon Celestial is the offensive pick; the auras are the defensive ones.
